title: Mama Bloom's Brood
paragraphs: Serialized Jewish-American domestic comedy centered on Becky and Jake Bloom, daughters Yetta and Sarah, and sons-in-law Harold and Sidney. The surviving story moves from family weddings and retirement plans into a cross-country automobile trip and an extended Hollywood/movie-business arc. Exact broadcast dates and original station schedule remain unresolved.
GRH documents the program through Surviving serialized family-comedy run (1934 to 1934).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family relationships and domestic life, parties, cards, restaurants and social leisure, money, business and investment, engagement, marriage and honeymoon, Hollywood and motion-picture business, and clothing, shopping and consumer goods.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Jewish-American family comedy on radio, Automobile vacation and cross-country mobility, and Hollywood as popular-culture destination.
